what: one judge over stored answers, gated on stored calibration answers in this file (app/eval/judge_stored.py)
does_not_show: that the judge is right on every kind of answer: the gate's reference is an exact-match label on single-value answers whose wrong class is a planted value of the same field, so a pass shows that the judge compares a single-value answer with the gold, not that it judges multi-part, paraphrased or computed answers correctly
an unbiased score where the judge's own weights generated the answers: such an answer set is marked `self_judged` (self-preference risk)
the truth where two judges agree: `agreement_with_stored_judges` is agreement between judges
grounding in the retrieved context: the correctness prompt shows the question, the gold answer and the answer only, and the M4 composite label is not collected
which answer is better: the AB/BA pairs compare an answer with its row's extractive answer in both orders to measure position bias, not quality

variance between runs or machines: one verdict per item at temperature 0 and seed 0; `segments` name the commit, GPU and time of each run that added verdicts, and a model whose prompt template carries the date may reply otherwise on another day
the judge's reasoning: a verdict stores the reply and the length of the reasoning the server returned, not the reasoning

protocol.gated_label: correctness verdict (app/eval/judge.py correctness_prompt: question, gold, answer; no retrieved context)
protocol.reference: exact_match_label, bounded (the gold may not sit inside a longer number or word)
protocol.abstention_rule: an answer that is NOT IN SOURCES and nothing else, to a question with a gold answer, is wrong by rule: no judge is asked, and the row is left out of kappa

failed.uncited_answer: a substantive answer with no citation: failed loud, not judged
failed.no_answer: an empty answer (nothing was delivered): counted, not judged

protocol.pairwise: AB and BA, the answer against the row's extractive answer: Which is better grounded and complete? Reply A, B, or TIE.

not_collected.composite: the M4 composite label (faithfulness, relevancy and groundedness with the retrieved context) is never gated or published and needs the retrieved chunks: not collected by a judge-only run

request.think: not sent: the server's default for the model
request.num_ctx: not sent: the server's context length

conditions.planted: the same chunks with every standalone occurrence of the gold value (numeric equivalents included) replaced, in memory, by another gold value of the same question template

calibration.planted_value_rule: the other gold values of the question's template (its text with digits replaced), distinct by value, sorted (numbers by value, words alphabetically): the next one after the gold, wrapping around

rows.gold: fusion on concatenates per-view features; fusion off uses the reference view only

rows.question: explain the difference between fusion on and fusion off
rows.gold: fusion on concatenates per-view features; fusion off uses the reference view only
rows.answer: When fusion is on, per-view features are concatenated before the depth head, whereas when it is off, only the reference view is used. Technically, the `project` function returns a concatenation of all features if `fusion_on` is true, but returns only the first feature if false.
